c.tagline: Home to the world's largest carved stone Buddha, watching over three rivers at the edge of the Sichuan Basin

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are metered but drivers rarely speak English; having your destination written in Chinese characters or using the DiDi app is essential

emergency.note: 110 for police, 120 for medical emergencies, 119 for fire - standard nationwide numbers; English-speaking operators are not guaranteed

avoid.reason: Unofficial 'guides' and overpriced boat touts near the Giant Buddha entrance — buy tickets only at official counters.

hood_desc: The riverside cliffs holding the 71-meter Leshan Giant Buddha, carved directly into the rock during the Tang dynasty. The surrounding park includes viewing platforms, Lingyun Temple, and steep stairways carved alongside the statue.
A wooded hill across the river from the Buddha, home to the ancient Wuyou Temple and its 1,000 carved arhat statues. Reached by bridge or boat, it's far less crowded than the main Buddha site.

Leshan's historic riverside streets, famous across Sichuan for snack stalls selling specialties like tofu pudding (dou fu nao) and grilled skewers. It's the best place to sample the city's celebrated street food scene at night.

The main riverside promenade in central Leshan, with parks, night markets, and views over the confluence of the Min, Dadu, and Qingyi rivers where the Buddha overlooks the water. Restaurants and hotels cluster along this strip.

The base town for Mount Emei, one of China's four sacred Buddhist mountains and a UNESCO World Heritage Site paired with the Giant Buddha. Cable cars and trails climb to temples and the Golden Summit, often above the clouds.

water.note: Boil or buy bottled water, as everywhere in China.

transit.pay: Cash, transit card, or WeChat/Alipay QR scan
transit.note: No metro; most visitors reach the Buddha via scenic-area shuttle bus or a sightseeing boat on the river

air: Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport (CTU) - main gateway, ~120km
Chengdu Tianfu International Airport (TFU) - newer hub, ~160km
train: Chengdu-Emeishan-Leshan high-speed rail, about 1 hour from Chengdu East
bus: Long-distance coaches from Chengdu Xinnanmen bus station, about 2 hours
ferry: Sightseeing boats on the Min River offer views of the Giant Buddha from the water

car.idp: Not recognized - China does not honor the IDP; self-drive is impractical for tourists, hire a licensed local driver instead

tip.r: Tipping is not part of local culture and can seem confusing to service staff; not expected in restaurants, taxis, or hotels

food.name: Qiaojiao niurou (propped-leg beef)
food.desc: Leshan's most famous dish: beef offal, tripe and brisket poached in a clear medicinal herb broth and dipped in dry chilli powder.

places.name: Gushixiang Qiaojiao Niurou
places.note: In the village where the dish was invented; the reference bowl for most locals.

places.name: Zhanggongqiao Food Street
places.note: The city's best-known eating street, with several long-running qiaojiao beef houses.

places.name: Jiaxing Road Food Street
places.note: Newer rival strip to Zhanggongqiao, busy with beef-broth restaurants at night.

food.name: Bobo ji (bowl-bowl chicken)
food.desc: Cold skewers of chicken, vegetables and offal steeped in a chilled chilli-and-sesame oil bath, picked from a clay bowl and paid for by the stick.

places.name: Ye Popo Bobo Ji
places.note: Intangible-heritage listed brand and the name locals cite first for bobo ji.

places.name: Zhanggongqiao Food Street
places.note: Multiple bobo ji counters side by side; pick the busiest and grab a basket.

places.name: Jiaxing Road Food Street
places.note: Late-opening skewer shops popular with Leshan students.

food.name: Tianpi ya (sweet-skin duck)
food.desc: Duck fried then lacquered with maltose syrup so the skin turns glassy and sweet while the meat stays savoury; sold by the half bird to take away.

places.name: Zhongji Tianpi Ya
places.note: Old-brand duck shop that shows up on every local sweet-skin duck list.

places.name: Zhanggongqiao Food Street
places.note: Duck stalls hang the glazed birds in the window; buy by weight, chopped to order.

food.name: Leshan doufunao
food.desc: Silky tofu curd in a starch-thickened spicy broth, loaded with crushed peanuts, pickles, coriander and often crisp fried noodles or beef.

places.name: Zhanggongqiao Food Street
places.note: Breakfast doufunao shops open early along the street; cheap and filling.

places.name: Jiaxing Road Food Street
places.note: Several tofu-curd specialists here serve it all day, not just at breakfast.

food.name: Niuhua malatang
food.desc: Leshan-style skewer hotpot from nearby Niuhua town, cooked in a numbing red broth and eaten stick by stick straight from the pot.

places.name: Niuhua Bapo Malatang
places.note: The best-known Niuhua malatang name, worth the short trip out of the city.

places.name: Zhanggongqiao Food Street
places.note: City-centre branches and imitators for those staying near the Giant Buddha.

food.name: Kaoyu (grilled river fish)
food.desc: Whole fish from the Min and Dadu rivers split, grilled, then simmered at the table in a tray of chilli, Sichuan pepper and vegetables.

places.name: Jiaxing Road Food Street
places.note: Grill-fish restaurants cluster here, busy from mid-evening onwards.

places.name: Jiazhou Changjuan riverside district
places.note: Riverside dining strip with grilled fish and night views toward the Buddha.

food.name: Emei green tea
food.desc: Zhuyeqing and other high-mountain green teas grown on Mount Emei just up the road, brewed leaf-in-glass and refilled all afternoon.

places.name: Jiazhou Changjuan riverside district
places.note: Teahouses with river views where a glass of green tea costs less than a coffee.

places.name: Teahouses near the Giant Buddha scenic area
places.note: Traditional bamboo-chair tea gardens, the Sichuan way to spend an afternoon.

food.name: Bingfen
food.desc: Chilled jelly made from fig seeds, served in a bowl of brown-sugar syrup with peanuts, raisins and rice balls; the local antidote to chilli heat.

places.name: Zhanggongqiao Food Street
places.note: Bingfen carts sit between the spicy stalls for exactly this reason.

places.name: Jiaxing Road Food Street
places.note: Dessert stands serve bingfen and liangxia rice-noodle drinks late into the night.

landmarks: Leshan Giant Buddha
The world's largest stone Buddha, a serene 71-meter Maitreya carved into the river cliff between 713 and 803, now a UNESCO World Heritage icon.
Lingyun Temple
The ancient hilltop monastery beside the Buddha's head, founded in the Tang dynasty, whose halls and incense smoke crown Lingyun Mountain.
Jiuqu Plank Road
A vertiginous staircase chiseled into the cliff beside the Giant Buddha, descending from crown to toes past niches of smaller carved figures.
Giant Buddha River Cruise (Sleeping Buddha view)
A boat trip on the Min River delivering the full frontal view of the colossus and the hill profile locals call the Sleeping Buddha.
Wuyou Temple
A tranquil Tang-era monastery on neighboring Wuyou Hill, its hall of 500 wildly expressive arhat statues among Sichuan's finest Buddhist art.
Mahao Cliff Tombs Museum
Han-dynasty cave tombs carved into the cliffs near the Buddha, displaying 1,800-year-old reliefs including an early image of the Buddha.
Oriental Buddha Park
A hillside park of thousands of Buddha statues including a 170-meter reclining figure, assembling replicas of Asia's great Buddhist sculpture.
Zhanggongqiao Food Street
Leshan's famous eating street, where locals queue for qiaojiao beef soup, sweet-skin duck and bobo chicken in one of Sichuan's great food towns.
Leshan Confucian Temple
A restored Confucian temple in the old city, with courtyards and shrine halls reflecting Leshan's history as a Sichuan administrative and scholarly centre.
Laoxiaoding
The tallest hill within Leshan's old city walls, now a park of pavilions and teahouses reached by a winding path from Moruo Square.

train.note: Leshan has no international trains - it sits well inland in southern Sichuan and the nearest border is more than a thousand kilometres away. Leshan Station is on the Chengdu-Leshan-Emeishan intercity high-speed railway, with frequent services from Chengdu East, Chengdu South and Shuangliu Airport station taking between 52 minutes and about 1 hour 20 minutes for around ¥54. The same line continues to Emeishan for the mountain, and connections at Chengdu East reach Chongqing, Xi'an and Kunming. Book on 12306 with your passport; the airport station stop makes this an unusually easy day trip straight off a flight.

bus.note: There are no international coach services. Long-distance buses arrive at the Leshan bus stations from Chengdu, Chongqing, Emei, Jiajiang, Kangding, Ya'an, Yibin and Zigong, and the Kangding and Ya'an services matter because those western Sichuan towns have no railway at all. For Chengdu and Emeishan the intercity train is faster and more comfortable, so the bus is mainly worth it for destinations off the rail network.

ferry.note: Leshan stands at the confluence of the Min, Dadu and Qingyi rivers but has no scheduled passenger ferry - the only boats are the sightseeing cruises that run out to view the Giant Buddha from the water, which sell tickets at the riverside pier and return to the same point.

half.name: Mount Emei Golden Summit
half.blurb: The UNESCO-listed sacred mountain an hour away, where a golden ten-directions Buddha statue rises above a sea of clouds at 3,077 meters.

half.name: Baoguo Temple
half.blurb: The gateway monastery at Mount Emei's foot, a 16th-century complex of gardens and halls that begins the pilgrim path up the sacred mountain.
